checks: Normalizing the projection of M preserves the ordinary volume law. For each s the homothet about a minimizing support point has ratio s and lies in the lower projection interval, giving F(s)>=s^d. Integrating its complement gives the centroid support distance.

Support and width are additive under the Minkowski sum, and the opposite threshold shifts cancel exactly in the sum of the two cap heights. This supplies the required width-weighted sum without replacing g_M by an endpoint-centroid average.
At least one cap height is at least its width divided by d+1. The corresponding upper-support homothet gives the direction-free guarantee, including if that cap is full.

For d>=2, a full endpoint suffices by (w_A+w_B)^d <= 2(w_A^p+w_B^p)^(d-1). Otherwise the nonnegative height ratios are below one, and the two upper-support homothets give their dth powers as fractions of the common endpoint volume a. Hölder applied to the weighted sum gives exactly W_d(R). A negative or zero ratio needs only the zero lower estimate, which includes the supporting-face case.
Matched 8407bedf6b42ff39 §4 (8) and f968b5a47e83bb95 §1 (2)–(4). Both occurrences of the directional bound have the identical true midpoint centroid, ordinary measure and exponent.

overlap.comparison: The accepted two-endpoint bound uses ordinary volume of the complementary middle cap, whereas the present estimate depends on the support widths and the centroid support distance. Neither part of the proof assumes an exact residual volume.

readability: Widths and cap heights are in the same units even when u is not a unit vector.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen statement and proof, followed by source and exact dependency comparison and exact rational checks where applicable.
summary: The support-height proof and the weighted Hölder step give both endpoint payments, with the same all-direction, all-shift scope including saturated cuts.
